components.explanation: Effect A scene: three GPUParticles3D (Flash, Sparks, Puff) under one Node3D, every setting from the brief, soft-dot GradientTexture2D in the scene; its config test and preview fixtures.
bullet_hit signal and emit in player.gd's fire path; impact_fx.gd pool of 12 under the level root (overlap, oldest restarted), wired in game.gd; the state test with real input.
Effect B scene: one GPUParticles3D with sphere emission, buoyancy and turbulence (influence tuned), config test and preview fixtures.
Presentation-only driver: health_changed/died in, emitting and amount_ratio out; the state test with real zombie damage, a medkit, pause and hide.
Godot 4.7.2's generated ParticleProcessMaterial shader (Puff duplicate), the dump tool, and the probe showing billboard particles drop the process scale.
Headless CPU cost script with an empty-scene control, and the windowed GPU-counter script.

func play(point: Vector3, normal: Vector3) -> void:
	var i := _free_index()
	if i < 0:
		i = order[0]
		recycled += 1
	order.erase(i)
	order.append(i)
	var b := pool[i]
	b.global_position = point
	b.global_basis = basis_y_to(normal)
	for e in b.get_children():
		(e as GPUParticles3D).restart()
	_started[i] = clock
	fired += 1
